name: West Germany
intro: It's 1948. Your cities are rubble, your country is split in four, your neighbors hate you, and the word "Germany" makes everyone reach for a rifle. You have one asset: everybody needs you. The Americans need a shield, the French need a market, the Soviets need you not to be in NATO. You're not sovereign yet. Play it right and you'll be Europe's richest country in twenty years. Play it wrong and you're a battlefield.

nodes.title: A State Half Built
nodes.situation: The West wants a separate West German state. Adenauer says yes; Schumacher's Social Democrats fear it locks in division. Stalin is blockading Berlin.

choices.label: Found the Federal Republic, Face West
choices.summary: Found the Federal Republic, Face West

effects.text: Basic Law, May 1949; a "provisional" capital that lasts 41 years
effects.insight: a state built to be temporary and outlived its purpose

effects.text: The GDR is founded in October in reply
effects.insight: two Germanies, each claiming to be the real one

effects.text: The Deutsche Mark launches the Wirtschaftswunder
effects.insight: a currency became a national identity

effects.text: France, terrified of a revived Germany, proposes the Coal and Steel Community
effects.insight: European integration starts as a leash on you

effects.text: Stalin lifts the blockade
effects.insight: he lost Berlin and gained a permanent grievance.

choices.label: Refuse a Separate State — Demand All-German Elections
choices.summary: Refuse a Separate State — Demand All-German Elections

effects.text: Four-power talks drag for years; no currency reform in the East
effects.insight: the whole country stays poor longer

effects.text: The US, needing a Western anchor, builds it in France and Italy instead
effects.insight: Germany is a bystander in NATO's founding

effects.text: Stalin dangles a neutral unified Germany (as he actually did in 1952)
effects.insight: this branch makes it real

effects.text: Adenauer loses to Schumacher
effects.insight: a Social Democratic, neutralist West Germany

effects.text: Austria and Germany become twin neutral states by 1955
effects.insight: a "Central European zone" the Rapacki Plan dreamed of.

choices.label: Found the State AND Demand Immediate Rearmament
choices.summary: Found the State AND Demand Immediate Rearmament

effects.text: France's Assembly explodes; the EDC is stillborn in 1949, not 1954
effects.insight: European integration is set back five years

effects.text: Stalin cites German rearmament to justify a permanent army in the GDR
effects.insight: the Cold War's front line hardens early

effects.text: Veterans' groups and old officers rush in
effects.insight: denazification collapses faster

effects.text: Truman refuses; the request embarrasses the occupiers
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: British Labour recoils
effects.insight: Britain distances from the German project for a decade.

nodes.title: The Stalin Note
nodes.situation: Stalin offers unification: a neutral, armed Germany with free elections, out of NATO. Adenauer says it's a trap; millions of Germans want to take it. The US wants you in a European army.

choices.label: Reject the Note, Join the West
choices.summary: Reject the Note, Join the West

effects.text: Adenauer wins 1953 on "no experiments"
effects.insight: Western integration becomes the FRG's DNA

effects.text: Stalin dies in 1953; the offer dies with him
effects.insight: historians still argue if it was real

effects.text: The June 1953 workers' uprising is crushed by Soviet tanks
effects.insight: East Germans learn nobody is coming

effects.text: The European Defense Community passes the German Bundestag, then dies in the French Assembly in 1954
effects.insight: NATO membership follows in 1955

effects.text: The US commits 250,000 troops to Germany for 40 years
effects.insight: you got a guarantee by giving up unity.

choices.label: Accept the Note — Test It
choices.summary: Accept the Note — Test It

effects.text: Four-power talks produce either a united neutral Germany by 1955 (historians' "what if") or a collapse that leaves you looking naïve
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

chance.failureText: The proposed outcome does not take hold in this run. Rival leaders resist the pressure; the uncertainty changes their next calculations.

effects.text: Eisenhower is furious; NATO loses its front line
effects.insight: the US considers withdrawing to the Rhine

effects.text: Even if sincere, Stalin's successors must agree
effects.insight: Beria (who actually floated a deal) is shot in 1953

effects.text: Poland, facing a united Germany, clings harder to Moscow
effects.insight: the Oder-Neisse border becomes the price

effects.text: France demands guarantees; the Franco-German reconciliation is delayed a decade.
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

nodes.title: Sovereign
nodes.situation: You're in NATO, sovereign, and offered the Treaty of Rome (EEC). The Hallstein Doctrine says you'll break relations with anyone who recognizes East Germany. Should you also want nuclear weapons?

choices.label: Join the EEC, Enforce Hallstein, No Own Nukes
choices.summary: Join the EEC, Enforce Hallstein, No Own Nukes

effects.text: Treaty of Rome, 1957
effects.insight: the Common Market makes you Europe's engine

effects.text: Yugoslavia recognizes the GDR in 1957; you cut ties
effects.insight: Hallstein costs you the Third World

effects.text: De Gaulle and Adenauer reconcile (1963 Élysée Treaty)
effects.insight: the Franco-German engine

effects.text: Adenauer wants "tactical" nukes anyway; the US says no, deploys its own under dual-key
effects.insight: Germany hosts the bombs it may not own

effects.text: Ulbricht, denied recognition, tightens the border; 200,000 flee yearly
effects.insight: the pressure that builds the Wall.

choices.label: Join the EEC AND Pursue a Franco-German-Italian Bomb…
choices.summary: Join the EEC AND Pursue a Franco-German-Italian Bomb (the real 1957 secret talks)

effects.text: De Gaulle takes power in 1958 and cancels the joint program (as he did)
effects.insight: or, at 40%, doesn't: a European bomb by 1965

effects.text: The US threatens to withdraw troops; Kennedy later offers the MLF to bury the idea
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

effects.text: Khrushchev's 1958 Berlin ultimatum comes harder
effects.insight: "German fingers on the trigger" is his best propaganda

effects.text: Poland's Rapacki Plan gains Western supporters
effects.insight: nuclear-free zone talks

effects.text: The SPD's "fight atomic death" campaign brings 1.5 million into the streets.
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

choices.summary: Drop Hallstein — Recognize Everyone, Trade With the East

effects.text: Recognition stabilizes the GDR; fewer flee; the Wall might never be needed
effects.insight: or comes anyway

effects.text: Third World ties bloom; German exports to Asia and Africa double by 1965
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Dulles is appalled; US–German trust dips
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.insight: Berlin is next.

nodes.title: The Wall
nodes.situation: East Germany is bleeding 2,000 people a day through Berlin. On August 13 barbed wire goes up overnight. Kennedy sends a battle group but won't tear it down. West Berliners feel abandoned. Adenauer stays in Bonn.

choices.label: Protest, Accept, Rely on the US
choices.summary: Protest, Accept, Rely on the US

effects.text: The Wall stands 28 years; 140+ die trying to cross
effects.insight: the Cold War's ugliest monument and its most stable border

effects.text: Adenauer's slow reaction costs the CDU its majority in 1961; Brandt's star rises
effects.insight: the Wall makes the man who'll take it down

effects.text: "Ich bin ein Berliner" 1963
effects.insight: Kennedy's guarantee is words and troops, not action

effects.text: Khrushchev, having solved his refugee problem, drops the Berlin ultimatum
effects.insight: the Wall was his defeat dressed as victory

effects.text: De Gaulle quietly notes the US won't fight for Berlin
effects.insight: he pulls France from NATO's command in 1966.

choices.label: Demand NATO Tear It Down
choices.summary: Demand NATO Tear It Down

effects.text: The October tank standoff (real) escalates; a US bulldozer meets Soviet armor
effects.insight: shots fired

effects.text: Kennedy refuses; the alliance splits publicly
effects.insight: Adenauer is called reckless

effects.text: Germans are terrified
effects.insight: the peace movement's first big march

effects.text: Khrushchev orders a second blockade
effects.insight: the airlift returns in 1962

effects.text: Khrushchev deploys missiles to Cuba as his counter-lever
effects.insight: the Cuban crisis gets an explicit Berlin price tag.

choices.label: Negotiate Directly With the GDR — "Small Steps"
choices.summary: Negotiate Directly With the GDR — "Small Steps"

effects.insight: expanded into a permanent arrangement

effects.text: Ulbricht, gaining a channel, loosens some travel
effects.insight: the Wall gets doors

effects.text: The US worries you're going neutral; aid is tied to loyalty
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Poland asks for the same channel
effects.insight: Eastern Europe's people-to-people contacts start early.

nodes.title: The Ten-Point Plan
nodes.situation: The Wall opened November 9. East Germans chant "We are one people." Gorbachev is wavering; Thatcher and Mitterrand are frightened; Bush is supportive. Kohl must decide how fast — and whether a united Germany stays in NATO.

choices.label: Fast Unification, Inside NATO, Pay Moscow
choices.summary: Fast Unification, Inside NATO, Pay Moscow

effects.text: October 3, 1990
effects.insight: one Germany, in NATO, with 380,000 Soviet troops paid to leave

effects.text: Gorbachev accepts DM 15 billion and a verbal assurance on NATO
effects.insight: the assurance is disputed for 30 years

effects.text: "One people" wins over reformers who wanted a better GDR
effects.insight: a state simply dissolves

effects.text: Mitterrand's price: the euro
effects.insight: a united Germany bound into a common currency

effects.text: The Oder-Neisse border is finally, formally recognized
effects.insight: Poland relaxes.

choices.label: Slow Confederation — Two States for a Decade
choices.summary: Slow Confederation — Two States for a Decade

effects.text: The GDR reforms as a separate democracy; economic collapse brings unification by 1995 anyway
effects.insight: messier, poorer

effects.text: Gorbachev is relieved; the August 1991 coup has one fewer grievance
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Thatcher is delighted; Kohl, not
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: The Bundestag's impatience with "wait" hands the 1990 election to a "unify now" challenger
effects.insight: Foreign decisions alter domestic coalitions. Leaders must answer to the institutions and people keeping them in power.

effects.text: No euro deal yet
effects.insight: the currency question waits.

choices.label: Unify Fast, Neutral, Out of NATO
choices.summary: Unify Fast, Neutral, Out of NATO

effects.text: A united, neutral Germany of 80 million
effects.insight: Europe's giant with no alliance

effects.text: Bush calls it the worst outcome; NATO's purpose is questioned
effects.insight: Partners judge a commitment by what it costs you to keep it. A changed commitment reshapes their choices.

effects.text: Gorbachev's dream
effects.insight: a Soviet win from a Soviet collapse

effects.text: Poland, stuck between a neutral Germany and a shaky USSR, begs for NATO
effects.insight: enlargement comes sooner

effects.text: France reconsiders its own NATO absence
effects.insight: and its bomb doctrine.
